passages.text: Send the tribute lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela in the desert to the mount of Daughter Zion.
passages.sermon:
Moab must send tribute.
Moab must send lambs as tribute.
The ruler of the land receives the tribute.
The lambs must come from Sela in the desert.
The lambs must go to the mount of Daughter Zion.
passages.original: שִׁלְחוּ־ כַ֥ר מֹשֵֽׁל־ אֶ֖רֶץ מִסֶּ֣לַע מִדְבָּ֑רָה אֶל־ הַ֖ר בַּת־ צִיּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Like fluttering birds pushed out of the nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon: “Give us counsel; render a decision. Shelter us at noonday with shade as dark as night. Hide the refugees; do not betray the one who flees.
passages.sermon:
The daughters of Moab are like birds.
These birds have been driven from their nest.
The daughters of Moab stand at the crossings of the Arnon River.
They are lost and scattered.
They say, “Give us advice.
Make a decision for us.
Give us shelter in the middle of the day.
Let your shade be as dark as night.
Hide those who are driven away.
Do not reveal the one who flees.”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֥ה כְעוֹף־ נוֹדֵ֖ד קֵ֣ן מְשֻׁלָּ֑ח תִּֽהְיֶ֙ינָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹת מוֹאָ֔ב מַעְבָּרֹ֖ת לְאַרְנֽוֹן׃ הָבִיאוּ עֵצָה֙ עֲשׂ֣וּ פְלִילָ֔ה שִׁ֧יתִי כַלַּ֛יִל צִלֵּ֖ךְ בְּת֣וֹךְ צָהֳרָ֑יִם סַתְּרִי֙ נִדָּחִ֔ים נֹדֵ֖ד אַל־ תְּגַלִּֽי׃

passages.text: Let my fugitives stay with you; be a refuge for Moab from the destroyer.” When the oppressor has gone, destruction has ceased, and the oppressors have vanished from the land, in loving devotion a throne will be established in the tent of David. A judge seeking justice and hastening righteousness will sit on it in faithfulness.
passages.sermon:
The fugitives from Moab will stay with you.
You must be a refuge for them.
Protect them from the destroyer.
The oppressor will be gone.
Destruction will end.
Those who trample others will disappear from the land.
A throne will be established in loving devotion.
This throne will stand in the tent of David.
A judge will sit on this throne.
He will rule with faithfulness.
He will seek justice.
He will act quickly to do what is right.
passages.original: יָג֤וּרוּ בָךְ֙ נִדָּחַ֔י מוֹאָ֛ב הֱוִי־ סֵ֥תֶר לָ֖מוֹ מִפְּנֵ֣י שׁוֹדֵ֑ד כִּֽי־ אָפֵ֤ס הַמֵּץ֙ כָּ֣לָה שֹׁ֔ד תַּ֥מּוּ רֹמֵ֖ס מִן־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃ וְהוּכַ֤ן בַּחֶ֙סֶד֙ כִּסֵּ֔א וְיָשַׁ֥ב עָלָ֛יו בֶּאֱמֶ֖ת בְּאֹ֣הֶל דָּוִ֑ד שֹׁפֵ֛ט וְדֹרֵ֥שׁ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּמְהִ֥ר צֶֽדֶק׃

passages.text: We have heard of Moab’s pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his overflowing arrogance. But his boasting is empty.
passages.sermon:
Moab is a nation.
Moab is very proud.
Moab is full of conceit.
Moab is extremely arrogant.
Moab boasts greatly.
We have heard about Moab’s pride and arrogance.
Moab’s boasting is empty.
Moab’s words are not true.
passages.original: שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ גְאוֹן־ מוֹאָ֖ב גֵּ֣א מְאֹ֑ד גַּאֲוָת֧וֹ וּגְאוֹנ֛וֹ וְעֶבְרָת֖וֹ לֹא־ כֵ֥ן בַּדָּֽיו׃ס

passages.text: Therefore let Moab wail; let them wail together for Moab. Moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, you who are utterly stricken.
passages.sermon:
Moab is a nation.
Moab is proud and arrogant.
Moab will suffer.
Therefore, Moab will wail.
All the people of Moab will wail together.
The people will mourn for Moab.
You who are stricken will moan.
You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן יְיֵלִ֥יל מוֹאָ֛ב לְמוֹאָ֖ב כֻּלֹּ֣ה יְיֵלִ֑יל לַאֲשִׁישֵׁ֧י קִיר־ חֲרֶ֛שֶׂת תֶּהְגּ֖וּ אַךְ־ נְכָאִֽים׃

passages.text: For the fields of Heshbon have withered, along with the grapevines of Sibmah. The rulers of the nations have trampled its choicest vines, which had reached as far as Jazer and spread toward the desert. Their shoots had spread out and passed over the sea.
passages.sermon:
The fields of Heshbon have withered.
The grapevines of Sibmah have also withered.
The rulers of the nations have trampled the best vines of Sibmah.
These vines had reached as far as Jazer.
The vines had spread toward the desert.
Their shoots had spread out.
Their shoots had passed over the sea.
passages.original: כִּ֣י שַׁדְמוֹת֩ חֶשְׁבּ֨וֹן אֻמְלָ֜ל גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֗ה בַּעֲלֵ֤י גוֹיִם֙ הָלְמ֣וּ שְׂרוּקֶּ֔יהָ עַד־ יַעְזֵ֥ר נָגָ֖עוּ תָּ֣עוּ מִדְבָּ֑ר שְׁלֻ֣חוֹתֶ֔יהָ נִטְּשׁ֖וּ עָ֥בְרוּ יָֽם׃

passages.text: So I weep with Jazer for the vines of Sibmah; I drench Heshbon and Elealeh with my tears. Triumphant shouts have fallen silent over your summer fruit and your harvest.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks these words.
Isaiah feels deep sorrow for Moab.
Isaiah weeps with Jazer.
He mourns for the vines of Sibmah.
Isaiah pours out his tears on Heshbon and Elealeh.
He grieves because joy has ended.
There are no more triumphant shouts over the summer fruit.
There are no more triumphant shouts over the harvest.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֡ן אֶבְכֶּ֞ה בִּבְכִ֤י יַעְזֵר֙ גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה אֲרַיָּ֙וֶךְ֙ דִּמְעָתִ֔י חֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וְאֶלְעָלֵ֑ה כִּ֧י עַל־ קֵיצֵ֛ךְ וְעַל־ קְצִירֵ֖ךְ הֵידָ֥ד נָפָֽל׃

passages.text: Joy and gladness are removed from the orchard; no one sings or shouts in the vineyards. No one tramples the grapes in the winepresses; I have put an end to the cheering.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Moab.
God removes joy and gladness from the orchards.
No one sings in the vineyards.
No one shouts in the vineyards.
No one tramples grapes in the winepresses.
God stops all cheering.
passages.original: וְנֶאֱסַ֨ף שִׂמְחָ֤ה וָגִיל֙ מִן־ הַכַּרְמֶ֔ל וּבַכְּרָמִ֥ים לֹֽא־ יְרֻנָּ֖ן לֹ֣א יְרֹעָ֑ע יַ֗יִן בַּיְקָבִ֛ים לֹֽא־ יִדְרֹ֥ךְ הַדֹּרֵ֖ךְ הֵידָ֥ד הִשְׁבַּֽתִּי׃

passages.text: Therefore my heart laments for Moab like a harp, my inmost being for Kir-heres.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks these words.
Isaiah feels deep sorrow for Moab.
His heart mourns for Moab.
His sorrow sounds like the music of a harp.
His inner being grieves for Kir-heres.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּן֙ מֵעַ֣י לְמוֹאָ֔ב כַּכִּנּ֖וֹר יֶֽהֱמ֑וּ וְקִרְבִּ֖י לְקִ֥יר חָֽרֶשׂ׃

passages.text: When Moab appears on the high place, when he wearies himself and enters his sanctuary to pray, it will do him no good.
passages.sermon:
Moab is a nation.
Moab goes up to the high place.
Moab becomes tired there.
Moab enters his sanctuary.
Moab tries to pray.
His prayer does not help him.
His effort does him no good.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֧ה כִֽי־ נִרְאָ֛ה כִּֽי־ נִלְאָ֥ה מוֹאָ֖ב עַל־ הַבָּמָ֑ה וּבָ֧א אֶל־ מִקְדָּשׁ֛וֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל וְלֹ֥א יוּכָֽל׃

passages.text: This is the message that the LORD spoke earlier concerning Moab.
passages.sermon: The LORD spoke a message about Moab long ago.\r\nThis is that message.
passages.original: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ מוֹאָ֖ב מֵאָֽז׃

passages.text: And now the LORD says, “In three years, as a hired worker counts the years, Moab’s splendor will become an object of contempt, with all her many people. And those who are left will be few and feeble.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking about Moab.
The LORD says this message now.
The LORD says, “In three years, this will happen.
A hired worker counts years carefully.
Count three years in the same way.
After three years, Moab will lose its splendor.
Many people live in Moab now.
But Moab’s glory will become shame.
Only a few people will remain in Moab.
The people who remain will be weak.
They will not be strong.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בְּשָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ כִּשְׁנֵ֣י שָׂכִ֔יר וְנִקְלָה֙ כְּב֣וֹד מוֹאָ֔ב בְּכֹ֖ל הֶהָמ֣וֹן הָרָ֑ב וּשְׁאָ֥ר מְעַ֛ט מִזְעָ֖ר ל֥וֹא כַבִּֽיר׃ס
